chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Aziz al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a slave boy owned by two men, one of whom married him off while the other was unaware, and then the other became aware afterwards: Is it for him to separate them? He said: 'For the one who did not know and did not give permission to separate them, and if he wishes, he may leave him in his marriage.'

key_terms.زَوَّجَهُ: He married him off (arranged marriage for the slave)
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: Slave (male), specifically a shared slave in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one co-owner of a slave marries him without the other co-owner's knowledge?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the rights of co-owners regarding the marriage of a shared slave, emphasizing that the unaware partner retains the unilateral right to annul or validate the union. It highlights the principle of consent in marital contracts within the context of *milk al-yaman* (ownership of the right hand), ensuring that one owner's action does not bind the other without their knowledge. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the intersection of property rights and personal status law.
